subject: gk
question:
Read the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R) carefully and choose the **correct **option.

**Assertion (A)**: India adopted import substitution during the planning era.

**Reason (R)**: This was to protect infant domestic industries from foreign competition.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Import substitution** refers to an economic policy aimed at reducing dependency on foreign goods by promoting domestic production and industries.
 
• India adopted the policy of import substitution during the planning era, particularly during the Second Five-Year Plan (1956-61) led by P.C. Mahalanobis, to boost industrialization.
 
• The primary objective was to protect the domestic industries, which were in their nascent stages, from foreign competition and to achieve self-reliance in industrial production.
 
• Through high import tariffs, quotas, and trade restrictions, foreign goods were made less competitive, encouraging the growth of Indian industries.
 
• While this policy played a critical role in laying the foundation for India’s industrial base, it also led to inefficiencies and a lack of competition in the long run.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First** FYP (1951-56): Focused on agriculture, controlling inflation, and refugee rehabilitation (Harrod-Domar model). 
 
• **Second **FYP (1956-61): Emphasized rapid industrialization, especially heavy industries (Mahalanobis Model). 
 
• **Third **FYP (1961-66): Aimed for food self-sufficiency and increased agricultural/industrial production, but faced challenges. 
 
• **Fifth **FYP (1974-78): Key focus on Garibi Hatao (poverty alleviation), employment, and social justice. 
 
• **Sixth **FYP (1980-85): Introduced early economic liberalization and aimed for technological self-reliance. 
 
• **Eighth **FYP (1992-97): Launched after the 1991 economic crisis, promoting LPG (Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation) and industrial modernization. 
 
• **Ninth **FYP (1997-2002): Focused on social sector development and equitable growth. 
 
• **Tenth **FYP (2002-07): Aimed for faster and more inclusive growth. 
 
• **Eleventh **FYP (2007-12): Focused on faster, more inclusive, and sustainable growth. 
 
• **Twelfth **FYP (2012-17): The final FYP, targeting faster, sustainable, and more inclusive growth with emphasis on education, infrastructure, and poverty reduction.
